aspects.says: Since Java 15 biased locking is off, so uncontended synchronized on old classes such as Vector, Hashtable and StringBuffer pays an atomic instruction again.
basis: section:A Removed JVM Option Is Ignored for a While, Then Stops the JVM From Starting
aspects.reason: a performance difference that needs a Java 15-era JVM and a benchmark to see; no deterministic test on the runner's JVM can observe it

aspects.says: With Nashorn removed in 15, ScriptEngineManager.getEngineByName returns null for a missing engine, so the failure appears where the engine is first used unless startup checks it.
basis: section:Nashorn Is Gone, and the Engine Lookup Returns null Instead of Failing

aspects.says: A HotSpot option is deprecated (works, warns), then obsolete (accepted and ignored, warns), then expired (unrecognized, the JVM refuses to start), each from the release named.
basis: section:A Removed JVM Option Is Ignored for a While, Then Stops the JVM From Starting

aspects.says: A preview feature needs --enable-preview with --release on javac, which marks the class file, and --enable-preview again on java, which otherwise refuses the class when it loads.
basis: section:Preview Features Must Be Switched On Twice, at Compile Time and at Run Time

aspects.says: A class file that uses preview features (minor version 65535) loads only on the release that compiled it, while an ordinary class loads on its release and every later one.
basis: section:A Preview Class File Runs Only on the Release That Compiled It

aspects.says: javac --release N checks code against N's API, so code using Nashorn's API compiles for 14 with a warning and fails on 21 with NoClassDefFoundError.
basis: section:Nashorn Is Gone, and the Engine Lookup Returns null Instead of Failing
aspects.reason: it shows only by compiling against an older --release and running on a newer JDK; a graded practice is compiled once, by the runner's own toolchain, against one release
